subject: defining uniform prior for the hyperparameter

messages.author: 25f786785d3ece32
messages.subject: defining uniform prior for the hyperparameter
parts:
Hello all
Please could you help me in defining uniform prior with 0, 100 for hyper parameter for iid random effect.

Additionally I want to know will it cause error as I read in one of the book that " Since INLA assumes that hyperparameters  are unbounded, it is difficult to set a uniform prior on the standard deviation in a bounded interval. "

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] defining uniform prior for the hyperparameter
parts:
you cannot define a bounded interval, also, there is not good reason for
doing that in my opinion.

you can define PC-prior,



https://projecteuclid.org/journals/statistical-science/volume-32/issue-1/Penalising-Model-Component-Complexity--A-Principled-Practical-Approach-to/10.1214/16-STS576.full

f(.., model="iid", hyper=list(prec=list(prior="pc.prec"param=c(A,0.01)))

then hyperpar is prec=1/sigma^2

Prob(sigma > A) = 0.01

and

SD(iid.effect) \approx 0.3*A

after prior is integrated out.

the prior is exponential, so with higher A, the rate is low, hence
alomost uniform.
